newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Saudi farm minister says '96 grain output 1.7 mln.
newsitem.headline: Saudi farm minister says '96 grain output 1.7 mln.

text.p: Saudi Arabia cut wheat and barley production to a total 1.7 million tonnes in 1996 from six million tonnes in 1992, newspapers quoted the agriculture minister as saying on Wednesday.

Minister of Agriculture and Water Abdullah bin Abdul-Aziz bin Muammar was quoted by Saudi newspapers as saying the cut was in line with efforts to reduce water use in the desert kingdom. He also said the kingdom no longer exported wheat.

Analysts estimate that Saudi Arabia produced some 1.2 million tonnes of wheat and around 450,000 tonnes of barley last year. Local wheat consumption is about 1.8 million tonnes. Analysts forecast barley imports this year of around six million tonnes.

The Arab News quoted Muammar as saying farm land area rose to 1.7 million hectares in 1995 from 60,000 in 1980 and that the kingdom had extended 27 billion riyals in interest-free loans to farmers between 1970 and 1995.
He said the ministry was trying to develop wheat and barley which would use less water.
The Arab News said the ministry was setting up a company to market Saudi farm output. "This Agriculture Marketing Company will be operational within the next two months," the minister said.
